approval_source.question_set: How the node's silent log::warn! lines reach the journal, how they are limited, and how long a send may wait while commit holds the execution lock
approval_source.selected_as: (b) Journal records (Recommended); 1/min per kind (Recommended); No wait (Recommended)

reason: The consensus application (dytallix-fast-node, consensus_stdio) passed five failures that never stop the node to the log crate: a snapshot chunk refused, a restored snapshot refused, a due snapshot not started, the snapshot writer failed, and metrics not recorded at a commit. No logger was ever installed, so log's maximum level stayed Off and every one was dropped. consensus_stdio's main() keeps the inherited journal socket (FD2) for bounded records only and adds no generic fallback onto it; the supervisor deliberately does not relay the application's FD2; stdout is the consensus protocol pipe.

decisions.question: How the warnings reach the journal
decisions.selected: Explicit journal records; the log dependency is removed
decisions.rule: Each of the five warnings is written as one bounded single-line JSON record, scope LOCAL_NODE_WARNING_V1 (schema 1, production_qualified false, release_authority false), with its kind, the warning's message bounded to 240 characters with control characters as spaces (as the helper failure record's error_text), warnings_total (the warnings of that kind since the process started) and unwritten_since_last_line. It is sent only to the inherited journal socket on FD2, non-blocking (MSG_DONTWAIT), and never to stdout, a pipe or a file. No log::Log logger is installed, and the application no longer depends on the log crate.

decisions.question: The rate limit
decisions.selected: At most one line a minute for each of three kinds
decisions.rule: STATE_SYNC_RESTORE (a snapshot chunk or the database restored from a snapshot refused; any peer offering a snapshot can cause one), SNAPSHOT_WRITE (a due snapshot not started, or its background writer failed) and METRICS (metrics not recorded at a commit) each have their own gate, separate from each other and from the admission line's: at most one line a minute per kind. Between lines a warning is counted, not written.

decisions.question: How long a send may wait
decisions.rule: A node warning line never waits for the journal. A line the journal takes nothing of is dropped at once, with no retry; a line it takes part of is finished within 5 ms or dropped. Either way the next line of that kind counts it in unwritten_since_last_line. The question named the two lines written while commit holds the execution lock (snapshot not started, metrics not recorded); the snapshot writer's own failure is reported from the same locked call (SnapshotWriter::start), and the rule applies to all five lines, the two state-sync lines included.

accepted_risks: Between lines, a warning's own message is not in the journal; the next line of its kind carries the count of those not written and its own message only.
A line the journal took part of and that is then dropped at its 5 ms deadline leaves a partial line, which the next write to the journal socket continues.
With a non-socket FD2 (development runs, test harnesses, pipes) nothing is written, as for the other records.
runtime-crypto's tracing::error! in verify_default and the jmt crate's tracing events are still dropped (no tracing subscriber is installed); the application does not call verify_default.
does_not_authorize: a log::Log logger or a tracing subscriber
any change to the helper failure record or the admission line (P01_E04_CHECKTX_HELPER_FAILURES_2026-11-05, P01_E04_CHECKTX_HELPER_RECORDS_2026-11-05)
a metrics counter or a monitor alert rule for these warnings, or any new monitor threshold value
any change to how a snapshot, a restore or metrics affect consensus (they still never do)
an automatic restart of the node unit (it stays Restart=no)
any run on a real host
